city.Gabon.description: This rainforest country sits right on the equator in Central Africa, along the Atlantic coast. Almost the whole land is thick jungle, and at Loango elephants, gorillas and hippos wander out onto the beaches.
city.Gabon.landmark: elephants strolling out of the jungle onto a wild Atlantic beach at Loango
city.Gabon.greeting: Most people speak French — say hello with “Bonjour” (bohn-ZHOOR).
city.Gabon.flag: traced a flag: three wide stripes of green, yellow and blue
city.Gabon.clue.0: planned a trip to a steamy rainforest country on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa
city.Gabon.clue.1: wanted to stand right on the equator, the invisible line around the middle of the Earth
city.Gabon.clue.2: kept talking about beaches where elephants and hippos stroll out of the jungle onto the sand
city.Gambia.description: This is the smallest country on mainland Africa — a thin ribbon of land following a river and almost completely wrapped by Senegal. Nicknamed the "Smiling Coast," it is a famous spot for watching hundreds of birds.
city.Gambia.landmark: wooden fishing pirogues on the wide Gambia River lined with mangroves and birds
city.Gambia.greeting: In Mandinka, a common hello is “I be nyaadi” (ee-beh-NYAA-dee).
city.Gambia.flag: red, blue and green stripes split by thin white lines
city.Gambia.clue.0: packed for a tiny sliver of a country on the coast of West Africa
city.Gambia.clue.1: packed binoculars to spot hundreds of colorful birds along the riverbanks
city.Gambia.clue.2: swapped travelers' cheques for a roll of dalasi
city.Ghana.description: This country on the coast of West Africa was once called the "Gold Coast" for its rich gold trade. It is famous for its brightly patterned kente cloth, its beloved football team, and huge Lake Volta.
city.Ghana.landmark: white walls of Cape Coast Castle above the crashing Atlantic surf
city.Ghana.greeting: English is official, but in Twi a warm welcome is “Akwaaba” (ah-KWAH-bah).
city.Ghana.flag: studied a flag in a guidebook: red, gold and green stripes with a single black star in the middle
city.Ghana.clue.0: couldn't stop admiring bright, patterned cloth woven in gold, green and red
city.Ghana.clue.1: talked about an old coast once so rich in gold that traders named it after the metal
city.Ghana.clue.2: packed a purse of leftover cedi
city.Guinea.description: Guinea is a green, tropical country on the coast of West Africa. It's known for lush forests where chimpanzees crack nuts with stones, busy trading markets, and mighty rivers that begin here and flow across the continent.
city.Guinea.landmark: plunging waterfall in the misty green highlands of Fouta Djallon
city.Guinea.greeting: French is the official language — say hello with “Bonjour” (bohn-ZHOOR).
city.Guinea.clue.0: asked about flights to a green West African country where great rivers are born and flow off across the continent
